description: A compact architecture fixture for a prerequisite-heavy mathematical and conceptual domain.

nodes.summary: Represent mutually exclusive outcomes, calculate probabilities, and distinguish a probability model from an observed result.

nodes.summary: Use wavelength, frequency, phase, and superposition to explain representative wave behavior.

nodes.summary: Represent simple amplitudes with complex numbers and connect amplitude magnitude to outcome probability.

nodes.summary: Predict and explain how alternative paths combine, when interference appears, and how measurement changes the prediction.

nodes.summary: Build simple outcome models, calculate predictions, then compare them with small observed samples without conflating model and result.

nodes.summary: Work through wavelength, frequency, phase, and superposition cases by predicting and sketching the combined behavior.

nodes.title: Probability model diagnostic
nodes.summary: A short offline diagnostic distinguishing model predictions from observed samples.

mastery.instructions: Answer both scenarios without hints or external calculation tools.

questions.prompt: For a fair six-sided die, what probability should the model assign to an even outcome?
A fair coin produced 14 heads in 20 trials. Which statement correctly separates the model from the observation?

options.label: The model remains 1/2; 14/20 describes this observed sample.
The observation disproves a fair-coin model.

nodes.title: Wave superposition analysis
nodes.summary: A worked explanation of representative phase and superposition changes.

mastery.instructions: Predict three pairs of waves with equal, opposite, and quarter-cycle phase differences. Sketch the sums and explain each result using phase and superposition.

nodes.title: Complex amplitude solution set
nodes.summary: A worked set connecting complex-amplitude sums to probabilities.

mastery.instructions: Solve three supplied two-amplitude cases, show the complex addition, compute magnitude squared, and explain what the result predicts.

nodes.title: Predict and explain an interference change
nodes.summary: A transfer-oriented explanation check for the target capability.

mastery.instructions: Given a two-path setup, predict how the observed pattern changes when path information becomes available. Explain the result using amplitudes rather than only naming the effect.

edges.rationale: Outcome probabilities are needed before connecting amplitudes to observed distributions.
Superposition and phase provide the physical foundation for interpreting an interference pattern.
The target explanation combines amplitudes for alternative paths before calculating probabilities.
The open text supplies probability language and worked quantitative context used by the guided scenarios.
The open text supplies wave, phase, and superposition background.
The linked text provides formal background and worked context.
The simulation makes changes in path and observation conditions visible.
Repeated model-versus-sample comparisons practice the observable probability capability.
Prediction and sketching make phase and superposition operational.
Worked cases connect complex addition to observable probability.
Prediction before observation practices causal explanation rather than recognition.
Both diagnostic scenarios must be solved correctly without hints.
The sketches and explanations demonstrate independent phase and superposition reasoning.
The worked set demonstrates amplitude calculation and interpretation.
The learner must predict and explain a changed condition, not merely recognize terminology.
